title: Picture shifts after ~33 h: core 1's 32-bit scanline count wraps at a non-multiple of 600
description: video.c numbers composed scanlines from power-on in a uint32_t (seq) and takes the frame line as seq % RASTER_ACTIVE_HEIGHT. 2^32 % 600 = 496, so at the wrap (2^32 lines / 36000 lines/s = 33.1 h, blanked time included: signal_off keeps counting) the composed line jumps from y 495 to y 0 while the DMA is at line 496: the whole picture is offset by 496 lines (status line drawn ~4 rows up, text wrapped round). A wake from blanking realigns it unless the wrap happened while blanked. Reported by the user: status line jumps several rows after days of worms with sleep/wake cycles. Fix: core 1 keeps the frame number and frame line in their own counters; seq only for differences and the ring index (LINE_BUFS divides 2^32).
notes: Fix on branch seq-wrap (src/video.c: frame_no/frame_y counters on core 1). Firmware with the fix flashed by the user 2026-10-10; soak test running for several days (wrap every 33.1 h). If the shift recurs, reopen this issue: the wrap explanation would then be incomplete.
close_reason: Fixed: frame and line counted apart from the wrapping scanline sequence. Hardware updated; soak test in progress.

title: Dropped/late lines in 132 columns while the CP/M side is CPU-heavy
description:
Reported by the user on hardware (2026-10-03, qol branch): in 132-column mode, with heavy CPU use on the CP/M side, display lines are starting to drop. Not yet measured.

Suspects (unverified):
- Core 1 composing too slowly in 132 columns: since qur.8 raster_compose reads each cell's bits from a packed bit string (raster_cell_bits: two byte loads, shift, mask per cell), and 132 is the layout with the most cells. Per-line budget is 10,560 cycles at 400 MHz; video_stats().late counts lines not composed in time (shown as stale pixels, sync is kept).
- SRAM bus contention: the Z80 (core 0) hammers its 160 KB of banks while core 1 reads raster rows, the palette and writes line buffers; check which SRAM banks/stripes these share and the bus priority of core 1 vs the DMA.
- Core 0 rendering bursts (video_update) are not involved in compose timing, but check that nothing on core 1 waits on core 0.
Next: measure first (qur status-line diagnostics issue, or a VIDEO_DIAG build: max encode cycles/line and late count on UART0), in 80, 80 full width and 132, idle vs CP/M CPU-bound (e.g. the Z80 exercisers or a tight loop). Fixes to weigh after: a faster 132 compose path (6-px cells: 4 cells per 3 bytes, or keep a byte per cell for 132 as before qur.8), core 1 bus priority (BUSCTRL), placing core 1's data in a separate SRAM bank (SCRATCH_X/Y or a dedicated striped region), compose further ahead (more line buffers).
notes:
2026-10-03: user sees it in 80 cols too, not only 132. Debug status line (qur.21) built for measuring. Leading hypothesis, not compose time: qur.8 made raster_render_line memset the slot's whole bits[] and then OR cells back in (packed rows share bytes); core 1 reads the slot live, so scanlines composed during a render show not-yet-redrawn cells blank (a partial or blank line for a frame). Before qur.8 each cell's byte was overwritten directly, so a line was never blank mid-render. Fonts read from flash (qur.8/9) make the window longer; more screen output from CP/M = more renders. Tell: 'late' stays 0 while lines drop, and 'render' us is in the hundreds. Fix candidate: render each stored row into a static 100-byte scratch and copy it in (or the whole line into a static raster_line_t, +2.5 KB). Compose estimate from the .dis: ~55-65 instr per cell, 132 cols ~70-85% of the 10560-cycle budget before IRQs/bus stalls: second suspect; the 'line' % will show it.
2026-10-03 measured (WORMS -c -n 20 -l 200 -d 0): 132 cols late 0, line 90/94%, render 207 us; 80 centred late 0, line 68%, render 192/543 us. Confirms render tearing, not compose. Fix done on qol (uncommitted, awaiting hardware): masked put_cell_bits, no memset; raster_select_font copies the layout's fonts from flash into a 20 KB SRAM pair (16-bit rows); 8x16 centred layout + 80 columns setting removed (user decision); FONT_132 variants removed (qur.14); per-cell font pick (qur.17). __end__ 0x2007dac4, ~9.3 KB free.
close_reason: Hardware-verified 2026-10-03: no dropouts; render 104 us (132) / 92 us (80), late 0

title: Bold text smears: 80-col bold 'm' turns into a solid block and touches its neighbours
description:
Reported on hardware (2026-10-03): in 80 columns a bold 'm' becomes a solid block and runs into the characters on either side.

Cause: raster_render_line (src/raster.c:35) emboldens by ORing each glyph row with itself shifted one pixel (m |= m << 1). Terminus 8x16 'm' has 1-px gaps between its three stems, so the shift fills them, and the smear reaches pixel 7, the blank column that separates the cell from the next one.

Fix options:
- 80 columns: use the real Terminus bold face (Uni2-TerminusBold16.psf.gz from console-setup, same family/licence/PSF loader) as a second 256-glyph table, chosen per cell for SCREEN_ATTR_BOLD. It costs 4 KB of SRAM (fonts are .data with COPY_TO_RAM; ~18.6 KB free on the qol branch). Connector glyphs (line drawing, blocks) keep the normal table so boxes still join.
- 132 columns: misc-fixed 6x12 has no bold face, so keep the smear but never fill the cell's last (gap) column, or skip it where it would close a 1-px gap.
- qur.8 (10x20 font) should use Uni2-TerminusBold20x10.psf.gz the same way.

Acceptance: test_raster checks a bold 'm' keeps its gaps and leaves the gap column clear; hardware check in 80 and 132 columns.
notes: 80 columns verified on hardware (bold faces). 132 columns still open: at 6 px a smeared bold m becomes a solid block; choosing a 132-column font with a bold face (see the conversation of 2026-10-03).

title: 80-column full-width option: Terminus 10x20 in 10-px cells filling 800x600
description:
Why: 80 columns uses 8-px cells and the 8x16 font, centred in 800x600 with 80 px black bars on both sides, and the 16-line glyph leaves 8 blank scanlines in each 24-line text row. A 10-px-wide font fills the screen with no video mode change: 80 x 10 = 800 px, clk_sys stays 400 MHz (same Z80 speed), and the monitor never resyncs. (Replaces the earlier idea of switching to 640x480 per column width. Pixel-stretching 8x16 to 10 wide was rejected: strokes come out 1 or 2 px depending on column.)

Font: Terminus 10x20 (Uni2-Terminus20x10.psf.gz from console-setup; same family, OFL licence and PSF loader as today's Uni2-Terminus16; 18x10 also exists). 20 glyph rows + 2 padding rows = 22 stored rows; glyph centred with 2 scanlines above and below.

Work:
- assets/fonts: add the PSF and note it in README/THIRD-PARTY.
- font_gen.py / cmake/fonts.cmake: emit 10-wide rows (two bytes per glyph row, or a packed form); the generated glyph ranges (DEC graphics, shades, blocks, box drawing 0x80-0x9F, control pictures) at 10 px; connectors must reach the cell edges.

That is less than today's 18 x 132 = 2376, so raster memory shrinks ~4 KB (SRAM is the tight resource, ~28 KB free). Bold (shift within 10 px), underline, blink, reverse, cursor inversion.
- raster_compose (core 1, __not_in_flash_func, no const/flash data): a 10-px path, 5 pixel pairs per cell; similar per-scanline work to 132 cols' 400 pairs; check video_stats().late on hardware.

- Docs: README, CLAUDE.md raster/font notes and resource budget.

title: Transfer device: port 10 (DMA) and src/xfer.[ch] on a FatFs /XFER folder
description:
Implements the Z80 side of qur.1's plan (see qur.1's design for the full protocol).

- machine.[ch]: port 10, high nibble command, low nibble volume (0 SD card, 1 USB): RESET 0x00, SETDMA 0x10 (+ two OUTs, low/high), FIND FIRST 0x20 / NEXT 0x30 (11-byte FCB pattern in; 11-byte name + 4-byte size out), OPEN 0x40, CREATE 0x50 (fails if it exists), READ 0x60 / WRITE 0x70 (128-byte record; reads ^Z-pad the last), CLOSE 0x80, CLOSE TEXT 0x90 (cut at the first ^Z of the last record, f_truncate), DELETE 0xA0. IN 10: 0 OK, 1 not found/end of list, 2 exists, 3 end of file, 4 I/O error, 5 no volume, 6 bad name/order. Records and names move via dma_read/dma_write (banking respected) and a 128-byte buffer; new platform hook uint8_t (*xfer)(uint8_t cmd, uint8_t volume, uint8_t buf[128]) (NULL: status 5). Port map comments.
- src/xfer.[ch] (portable, FatFs): the hook: <vol>:/XFER (made on the first CREATE), FCB <-> 8.3 names, ? matching, names CP/M cannot take skipped, one FIL + one DIR (FIND NEXT keeps its place while a file is open). RESET on machine reset, monitor entry and the monitor's card re-check. Wired into main.c's CP/M platform and test_machine's host platform.

Acceptance: test_machine round-trips a text and a binary file through /XFER, via the xfer API and via port 10 from Z80 code; wildcards; CREATE on an existing file; DELETE; CLOSE TEXT; missing card (status 5); RESET closes an open file. SRAM measured (expected < 0.5 KB).
close_reason: Port 10 + src/xfer.[ch] done 2026-10-04: test_xfer (9 tests, FAT12 RAM volume) and test_machine's port test (Z80 code, banked DMA) pass; ~2.3 KB SRAM. On hardware with qur.26's tools.

title: Plan: moving files into and out of the CP/M machine without pulling the SD card
description:
Why: all machine data lives in .DSK images on the one SD card, so getting a file in or out today means power off, pull the card and use image tools (cpmtools etc.) on a PC. Planning ticket: decide the design, then file/adjust the implementation tickets under qur.

Questions to settle:
- Media: (a) a folder on the existing SD card (fz80-style IMPORT/EXPORT folders; still needs a card pull to reach the PC, so only half a fix), (b) USB mass storage on the host port next to the keyboard (best long term; hot-pluggable, no machine shutdown), (c) a second SD slot on SPI1 (free pins GP8-11). Recommendation to evaluate: build the Z80-side interface against FatFs paths so the media is just a volume (0: SD, 1: USB), do (a) first, then (b).
- Z80 interface: a new port device (machine.c, like port 8) with a command/status/data protocol (fz80-firmware/firmware/fZ80.7/SDz.h has SVC_IMPORT/EXPORT/IMLIST/EXLIST as a reference) vs. mapping a FAT directory as a CP/M drive (much harder: CP/M directory emulation).
- CP/M tools: e.g. IMPORT.COM / EXPORT.COM / a DIR-like lister, written in Z80 asm like worms.asm, assembled at build time and put on CPM22 by diskimg_gen.py --file.
- 8.3 name mapping (no LFN in ffconf), user areas, text vs binary (^Z padding to 128-byte records, trimming on export), wildcards, overwrite rules.
- Coexistence with drives.c keeping images open on the same volume, and the 250 ms write flush.
- SRAM budget (~28 KB free): FatFs FIL objects, buffers; TinyUSB MSC host class cost.
- Alternatives worth one line each in the decision: XMODEM over SIO2/UART0, or the host tools/hostbridge.py path.
design:
# File transfer for the CP/M machine (qur.1 plan, 2026-10-03)

Goal: copy files between CP/M disks and plain FAT files without image tools
on a PC: first through a folder on the SD card, then a USB stick plugged in
while the machine runs.

## Decisions

- Media: a folder on the SD card first (volume 0), a USB stick next (FatFs
  volume 1, qur.3). No second SD slot.
- One folder per volume, /XFER (created on the first export). [default;
  alternative: fz80-style /IMPORT + /EXPORT]
- Z80 side: a port device with DMA, in the style of the disk controller
  (port 4): set a DMA address once, then each command moves a whole
  128-byte record or a name to/from Z80 memory. Not a memory-mapped bank
  (banking would swap out the tool's own TPA; a device bank would cost
  every memory access), not a CP/M drive emulated over FAT.
- CP/M tools in Z80 assembly, built at build time like worms.asm and put on
  CPM22: XLS (list a transfer folder) and XPIP (copy, roughly PIP's
  syntax). The FAT side is named like a PIP device: SD: (the card's
  /XFER) and USB: (the stick's /XFER, with qur.3).
- z80pack's XDIR.COM is removed from CPM22: it only works on drives A and
  B (by design: "ERROR - SELECT DRIVE A OR B"); DIR and STAT cover all
  drives.
- Records: copying to CP/M pads the last partial record with ^Z; copying
  to SD:/USB: writes whole records, [T] cuts at the first ^Z of the last
  record. As PIP, an existing destination file is replaced.
- Alternatives left out: XMODEM over SIO2 with PCGET/PCPUT (needs a PC on
  UART0; could be added to the disk later), tools/hostbridge.py (terminal
  mode only).

## Port 10: the transfer device (ours, like port 8)

OUT 10 = command, IN 10 = status of the last command. High nibble the
command, low nibble the volume (0 SD card, 1 USB), as the FDC puts the
drive in its low nibble.

| Cmd | Name | DMA buffer |
|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | RESET | close the file and the listing |
| 0x10 | SETDMA | the next two OUTs to port 10: address low, high |
| 0x20 | FIND FIRST | in: 11-byte FCB pattern ("NAME    EXT", ? wildcards); out: 11-byte name + 4-byte size (LE) |
| 0x30 | FIND NEXT | out: as FIND FIRST |
| 0x40 | OPEN | in: 11-byte name; open /XFER/NAME.EXT to read |
| 0x50 | CREATE | in: 11-byte name; new file, fails if it exists |
| 0x60 | READ | out: the next 128-byte record (^Z-padded at the end) |
| 0x70 | WRITE | in: a 128-byte record |
| 0x80 | CLOSE | flush and close |
| 0x90 | CLOSE TEXT | as CLOSE, cut at the first ^Z of the last record |
| 0xA0 | DELETE | in: 11-byte name |

Status: 0 OK, 1 not found / end of list, 2 exists, 3 end of file, 4 I/O
error, 5 no volume (no card, no USB stick), 6 bad name or command out of
order.

- Names are the CP/M FCB form, so a tool passes the CCP's parsed FCB at
  005Ch straight through (the CCP already turns * into ?s).
- FAT names: 8.3 only (no LFN in ffconf); a PC's long names appear as their
  short forms (LONGFI~1.TXT). Names with characters CP/M cannot take are
  skipped by FIND.
- One open file and one listing at a time; FIND NEXT keeps its place while
  a file is open (XPIP lists and copies in one pass).
- RESET on machine reset, monitor entry and the monitor's card re-check, so
  no file stays open across them.

## Code

- src/machine.[ch]: port 10 state machine (SETDMA bytes, command
  dispatch), copies records and names between Z80 memory (dma_read /
  dma_write, banking respected) and a 128-byte buffer, and calls a new
  platform hook: uint8_t (*xfer)(uint8_t cmd, uint8_t volume, uint8_t
  buf[128]) (NULL: status 5). Port map comment updated.
- src/xfer.[ch] (portable, FatFs): the hook's implementation: /XFER paths
  per volume, FCB name <-> 8.3 conversion, pattern matching, the open FIL
  and DIR, padding and ^Z cutting (f_truncate). Wired into main.c's CP/M
  platform and test_machine's host platform.
- src/cpm/xfer.inc: port and command constants, shared helpers (print,
  numbers, a command-tail parser for "d:", "SD:", "USB:", names with
  * and ? into FCB form, and [options]).
- src/cpm/xls.asm: XLS [SD:|USB:][afn]: names and sizes in the folder
  (default SD:, *.*).
- src/cpm/xpip.asm: XPIP dest=source [T], one side a CP/M drive, the
  other SD: or USB:. The CCP's FCBs cannot hold SD:/USB:, so XPIP parses
  the tail at 0080h itself.
    XPIP SD:=B:*.TXT          CP/M -> card, names kept
    XPIP A:=SD:*.COM          card -> CP/M, names kept
    XPIP SD:NEW.TXT=OLD.TXT   one file, renamed (default drive)
    XPIP B:LOG.TXT=SD:LOG.TXT[T]  (T only matters towards SD:/USB:)
  A wildcard source needs a drive or SD:/USB: alone as the destination.
  To CP/M: device FIND FIRST/NEXT, per match BDOS delete + make, device
  OPEN, READ -> BDOS write sequential, close both. To the card: BDOS
  search first/next collects the names first (opening files disturbs the
  search), then per file device DELETE + CREATE, BDOS read sequential ->
  device WRITE, CLOSE or CLOSE TEXT. Prints each name; stops on a full
  disk or an I/O error.
- src/diskimg_gen.py: --delete NAME CPMNAME (free a file's directory
  entries on an 8" image), used for XDIR.COM on CPM22.
- src/cpm/build.sh + cmake/diskimg.cmake: assemble XLS and XPIP, --file
  them onto CPM22, --delete XDIR.COM.
- README: a "Moving files" section.

## Costs

- SRAM: one FIL and one DIR (small with FF_FS_TINY), a 128-byte buffer,
  names: under 0.5 KB. USB later: a second FATFS (~0.6 KB) plus TinyUSB's
  MSC host (to measure).
- Flash: three small .COM files on CPM22 (a few KB compressed).
- Time: file work runs inside the Z80's port access, within its slice; a
  record is mostly buffered by FatFs. Video (core 1) is not involved.

## Tickets

title: Settings lost on reflash: UF2 E10 block erases the last flash sector

title: Disk controller: refuse I/O to a hard-disk image until the running OS has asked port 8 for its format
description:
picosim's BIOSes (CP/M 3's BNKBIOS3, MP/M) treat every drive as an 8" floppy and never ask port 8; floppy track/sector numbers fit inside a 4/8 MB image's geometry, so the controller accepts them and DIR shows garbage while writes overwrite parts of the image (e.g. C:/D: left mounted from CP/M 2.2 in DRIVES.CFG, then booting CPM3-1).

Guard, OS-agnostic (no CP/M 2.2/3 setting): machine.c remembers per drive whether port 8 has been asked for its format since the last machine reset; FDC reads/writes to a drive holding a hard-disk image return a disk error until it has. Floppies unchanged. Our CP/M 2.2 BIOS asks at every SELDSK, so it is unaffected; our CP/M 3 BIOS (f8w.4) will ask too. Reset clears it (also the monitor's remount: a new image needs asking again). Tests in test_machine: an HD on C: under a BIOS that does not ask -> error, never a write; under our 2.2 BIOS -> works.

title: Our banked CP/M 3 BIOS: drives A-H, port 8 formats (8" / 4 MB / 8 MB HD)
description:
picosim's BNKBIOS3 (cpm3gen.dsk BNKBIOS3.ASM, srccpm3/bnkbios3.asm upstream) has four drives A-D, all 8" floppies, and never asks port 8: hard-disk images are unusable (f8w.7 makes them an error instead of corruption) and E-H are invisible. Patch it (start from picosim's, keep its console/clock/MMU code):
- 8 drives A-H; at SELDSK ask port 8 for the image's format (as src/cpm/bios.asm does) and point the DPH at the floppy, 4 MB or 8 MB DPB; no image -> select error. CP/M 3 DPB adds PSH/PHM (0: 128-byte sectors).
- CP/M 3 DPH fields per drive: XLT (floppy skew only), MF, DIRBCB, DTABCB, HASH, HBANK; allocation vectors (double-bit for GENCPM's default: 8 MB HD 2040 blocks -> 510 bytes) and checksum vectors (floppies only).
- Memory: directory hash tables (1024 entries x 4 bytes = 4 KB per HD drive) and buffers placed by GENCPM (GENCPM.DAT answers): bank 0 vs common vs bank 2 (HBANK). Keep the TPA at 61K or better.
- Boot stays from a floppy on A: (bootable HDs deferred, f8w.5): picosim's boot sector, CPMLDR and LDRBIOS stay as they are; only CPM3.SYS changes (GENCPM link of our BNKBIOS3.SPR with RESBDOS3/BNKBDOS3), written onto our built-in CPM3-1 image in place of picosim's.
- Clock: ports 65/66 as picosim's.
Tests (test_machine): boot CPM3-1 with floppies and 4/8 MB images on A:-H:; DIR, PIP a file onto an HD drive and back, warm boot (^C), SETDEF across drives.
notes: Done on cpm3-bios (uncommitted). Differs from the plan: no hashing (picosim's DPHs have it off), so no bank 2; DPBs must be in common memory (BDOS fn 31 gives SHOW their address); HD CKS 0, not 8000H (the BDOS ignores media change on permanent drives); READ/WRITE return 0FFH media changed when port 8's format or new mount count (second IN, drives_mounts) differs from log-in; GENCPM MEMSEG00 00,77,00; TPA 61K (RESBDOS F600, a page more than picosim).

title: CP/M 3 on the Z80 machine: built-in disks, our tools, our banked BIOS (drives A-H, hard disks)
description:
Banked CP/M 3 (CP/M Plus) as a second OS for the CP/M machine: SETDEF drive search, SYS files across user areas, the user number in the prompt, date/time. First real user of the MMU banks (MACHINE_BANKS=2, 96 KB of SRAM).

Found 2026-10-13: z80pack picosim's cpm3-1.dsk/cpm3-2.dsk (upstream 91fd28e, the commit we vendor) boot unchanged on our machine (host harness: CPMLDR -> BNKBIOS3/BNKBDOS3 into banks via port 64, 61K TPA, PROFILE.SUB runs SETDEF, DATE answers from ports 65/66, USER 3 -> 3A>). Our port map is a superset of picosim's (0/1, 4, 64, 65/66, 255 error LEDs). Not yet tried on hardware.

How it boots: the FF00 boot ROM reads track 0 sector 1 of A:; picosim's boot.asm loads 25 sectors (CPMLDR + LDRBIOS) to 0100H; CPMLDR reads the file CPM3.SYS (GENCPM's link of BNKBIOS3.SPR, RESBDOS3, BNKBDOS3); CCP.COM is a file reloaded on warm boot. A CP/M 3 BIOS cannot run under the 2.2 BDOS or vice versa (DPH/DPB layouts, entries 18-33), so each OS keeps its own BIOS.

picosim's BNKBIOS3 has 4 drives (A-D), 8" floppy only, no port 8: hard-disk images and drives E-H need our own BIOS. cpm3gen.dsk has the sources/RELs (BNKBIOS3.ASM, LDRBIOS.ASM, SCB, GENCPM.DAT, CPMLDR.SUB, SYSGEN.SUB); cpm3-2.dsk has RMAC, LINK, GENCPM.

title: Scrolling shows the line that left in the recycled row until the next render
description:
Reported by the user 2026-10-04: transient artifacts while scrolling. screen_scroll_up/down rotate row_map so the slot leaving one end is reused at the other, then clear its cells (fill_slot) and mark it dirty. Core 1 draws from raster[slot] (core 0's rendered pixels), not the cells, so from the remap until video_update re-renders the slot the new row shows the old line's pixels. Several scrolls can land between renders (CP/M: 10-25 per 10 ms slice under TYPE, hundreds for empty lines; terminal: up to 256 bytes per pass), giving a band of stale rows for up to a frame.

Fix: clear the cells before the slot is attached at the other end (fill_slot before the remap), and blank its rendered pixels at once through a screen recycle hook that video.c sets (raster_blank_line: zero bits, fg = bg = the colour the new row shows, reverse video included), so a recycled row shows blank until video_update draws it. Optional later: latch row_map per frame on core 1 (a mid-frame scroll can mix two mappings).
close_reason: Hardware-checked 2026-10-04

title: Keyboard dead after idle + screen blank, then plugging in a USB stick; replugging the keyboard does not recover
description:
Seen once on hardware, 2026-10-04, with the qur.3 build (USB sticks; LED report deferred out of tuh_hid_mount_cb). Not reproduced since.

What happened: left idle at least 5 minutes, the screen blanked (Blank after), woke with an ordinary key, then plugged a USB stick into the hub (keyboard on the same hub): the keyboard stopped responding. Replugging the keyboard did not bring it back. The cursor kept blinking and the CP/M status line (MHz field) was still drawn, but the cursor is core 1 (video), so core 0 being alive is not established; whether the MHz value still changed is unknown.

What is known to work (same build): hot-plugging the keyboard through the hub in every order (same port, another port, direct, hub back), the stick appearing as USB: with its LED on, XLS USB:, XPIP both ways. A normal start-up logs: 1s led1, 1s msc2, 1s up2, 10s vol2 (the stick takes ~10 s to be ready; the mount waits for it).

Suspects (unverified):
1. Core 0 stuck waiting on the stick: usbmsc io_wait runs tuh_task until a transfer completes, with a 3 s timeout per transfer; a stick that keeps timing out could hold the main loop for long stretches (keys queue but nothing reacts). Debug usb would show 'timeout' events and/or a frozen clock.
2. The LED report colliding with a new device's set-up at address 0: usbkbd's usb_quiet only checks devices that have an address, so an LED SET_REPORT can still start while a just-plugged device's first control requests (at address 0) are under way; TinyUSB has one control transfer for the whole host (see CLAUDE.md), and a lost enumeration request leaves it 'enumerating' for good. But the keyboard should then still type, which does not fit.
3. TinyUSB 0.18's RP2350 host driver: a low-speed keyboard behind a full-speed hub (preamble) mixed with the stick's bulk transfers; a timing problem that the earlier tests dodged.
4. Something tied to the long idle or the blank/wake (no USB code depends on either, as far as known).

Troubleshooting in place (in the firmware):
- SET-UP Status line = 'debug usb': ' <uptime>s | usb: <last 4 events>'. If the uptime stops, the main loop (keyboard, USB, CP/M) has stopped. Events: up/down (device set up / gone), kbd/kbd- (keyboard), msc/msc- (stick), vol/vol?/unvol (USB: mounted / not mountable / unmounted), timeout/gone/ioerr/busy (stick transfer >3 s / stick pulled / failed / refused), led/led? (keyboard LEDs sent / refused), xN for repeats.

title: Escape parser stuck in an unterminated OSC/DCS string: end strings on CR/LF (xterm brokenStringTerm) plus a length limit
description:
Why: the escape parser can get stuck discarding a string forever, and then the screen stops updating. ESC ] (OSC) and ESC P / ESC X / ESC ^ / ESC _ (DCS, SOS, PM, APC) put vtparse in OSC_STRING (src/vtparse.c:198) or STRING (src/vtparse.c:203). It leaves only on ESC, CAN or SUB, plus BEL for OSC. There is no length limit and no timeout, and the 8-bit ST (0x9C) is ignored because c1_controls is off (src/vtparse.c:92). After that, every printable byte is thrown away.

It is easy to trigger by accident. Alt-modified keys send a bare ESC prefix (src/keyboard.c:233-235), so Alt+], Alt+Shift+P, Alt+Shift+X, Alt+Shift+6 (^) and Alt+Shift+- (_) each open a string. So does any CP/M program that echoes an ESC-prefixed key it read, or a host that sends a truncated sequence. F11 (dmt.34) and SET-UP R (dmt.35) now get you out of it, but nothing stops it from happening.

What, after xterm's brokenStringTerm resource. XTerm Control Sequences (patch #411) describes it as "exit string mode if it decodes a common control character such as carriage return before the string terminator"; it is xterm's workaround for programs that leave strings unterminated:

1. In OSC_STRING and STRING, a C0 control other than BEL (in OSC) ends the string and goes back to GROUND. At least CR and LF should do this; most likely every C0 except BEL should. The control is then executed as usual, so the CR or LF still takes effect. This terminal discards the contents of every string anyway, and none of the strings it is likely to receive contain C0 controls (window titles, OSC 52 base64, DECRQSS, sixel), so nothing is lost. With this rule, pressing Return after an accidental Alt+] fixes things straight away.
2. As a backstop, limit the length of a discarded string (a counter in vtparse_t; for example 512 or 1024 bytes, which is about GNU screen's 768). At the limit, go back to GROUND; the rest of the string then prints as text. Other programs use limits like this (screen 768, xterm.js 10 MB, Emacs xterm-max-cut-length "to protect users from runaway sequences"). Keep it well above the longest string a host is likely to send to this terminal.
3. Optional, separate decision: accept 8-bit ST (0x9C) as a string terminator even when c1_controls is off. It is never a UTF-8 lead byte, but it can be a UTF-8 continuation byte, so it could end a string early. Leaving this out is fine.

Out of scope: Alt sending an ESC prefix is standard (xterm metaSendsEscape) and stays as it is.

Tests (test/test_vtparse.c and test/test_term.c):
- ESC ] text CR, then more text: the later text prints and the CR takes effect.
- ESC P with no terminator, then LF: the parser is back in GROUND.
- OSC still ends on BEL and on ESC \; existing test_ignored_sequences still passes.
- A string longer than the limit goes back to GROUND at the limit; vtparse_reset() and each new string clear the counter.
- Sixel-like DCS data with no C0 controls is still discarded completely up to ESC \.
- README Limitations or terminal section: note the behaviour.
notes: 2026-10-12 on branch parser-setup-fixes (uncommitted): vtparse OSC_STRING/STRING end on any C0 but NUL (BEL still OSC's silent terminator; the C0 then executes) and after VTPARSE_MAX_STRING=1024 bytes (string_len in vtparse_t, reset by clear()). Tests: test_vtparse test_unterminated_strings, test_term test_unterminated_string_ends_on_control. README Limitations. Hardware check: Alt+] then Return.

title: F11 in CP/M mode should reset the terminal, not just the Z80 machine
description:
Why (reported by the user): "a reset through F11 does not reset the colors/terminal state when it should". In CP/M mode F11 goes reset_key() (src/main.c:449) -> cpm_reset() (src/main.c:640), which flushes the drives, drops the typed-ahead key queue and calls machine_reset() - but never touches term_t. So leftover SGR / DECSCNM / DECCOLM / origin mode / scrolling region survive a reset, and a program that left fg == bg stays unreadable. F11 is expected to act like the reset button of a real machine, which would also reset the terminal.

The freeze this was seen with: cpm_reset() prints "*** Reset" and reboots the Z80, and the rebooted program sends its init sequences (worms.asm SINIT = ESC [ 0 m ESC [ ? 25 l ESC [ 2 J), so a full reboot normally clears the colours. It does not when the escape parser is wedged - see dmt.33.

What: in cpm_reset() (src/main.c:640), call term_reset() after machine_reset() and before term_puts("\r\n*** Reset\r\n"), so the banner and the rebooted program start from a known state. Needs dmt.33 for the term_reset() API.

Terminal mode is deliberately out of scope: F11 there is a function key sent to the host as ESC [ 2 3 ~ (src/keyboard.c:76, src/keyboard.c:205-206) and the escape hatch for that mode is the SET-UP R reboot - tracked separately.
notes: Implemented: cpm_reset() calls term_reset() before the drive-A check (so the monitor path is reset too) and, per the user, switches back to the SET-UP width (default_columns, the last applied Columns setting, set in apply_settings) via term_set_columns when it differs; the status line redraws through screen_resets. README F11 and Columns rows updated. Awaiting hardware check: in CP/M, leave colours/DECSCNM/132 cols/wedged ESC ] then F11.

title: Add term_reset(): a public terminal reset that also clears the escape parser
description:
Why: after a freeze the terminal has no local reset at all. reset() is static in src/term.c:214 and there is no API to force one, so nothing can clear leftover SGR colours, DECSCNM, DECCOLM, origin mode or a scrolling region from outside. RIS (ESC c, src/term.c:550) also does not reset the vtparse state, so a host reset cannot recover a wedged parser.

What:
1. Add void term_reset(term_t *t) to src/term.h. Implement in term.c by exposing the existing static reset(), then calling sync_cursor() so screen->cursor_col/row are refreshed.
2. Route RIS (esc_dispatch case 'c', src/term.c:550) through term_reset().
3. reset() should clear t->last_char: after a reset REP (CSI b, src/term.c:464) can currently repeat the character printed just before it.

Related (not in this issue): term_reset() is what lets a user recover from a wedged parser, but it does not prevent the wedge. vtparse can sit in STRING (src/vtparse.c:198) or OSC_STRING (src/vtparse.c:193) forever - entered by ESC P / ESC X / ESC ^ / ESC _ / ESC ] - with no length bound and no timeout, and 8-bit ST (0x9C) is ignored because c1_controls is off (src/vtparse.c:86). Alt-modified keys emit a bare ESC prefix (src/keyboard.c:233-237), so Alt+], Alt+Shift+P, Alt+Shift+X, Alt+Shift+6 and Alt+Ctrl+/ all trigger it, as does any CP/M program that echoes an ESC-prefixed key it read. See the VT510 RM ch.4 behaviour ("ignores all following characters until it receives a SUB, ST, or any other C1 control character") and note xterm et al. rely on a length bound - Emacs ships xterm-max-cut-length for exactly this. Tracked separately.

Tests (test/test_term.c): term_reset restores default fg/bg after SGR 30;40m plus reverse, clears DECSCNM, resets margins and origin mode, homes the cursor, shows the cursor, and recovers the screen after a wedged ESC ].
notes: Implemented: vtparse_reset() (back to GROUND, keeps callback/c1_controls, safe from the callback); public term_reset() = vtparse_reset + reset + sync_cursor; RIS goes through it; reset() clears last_char. Width deliberately not touched by term_reset/RIS (host ESC c keeps width, as xterm). Tests: test_term_reset, test_term_reset_recovers_wedged_parser (OSC, DCS, mid-CSI), test_reset_forgets_rep_char, vtparse test_reset. Awaiting hardware check together with dmt.34.

title: Palette-indexed cell colours: xterm-256 palette table on core 1, swappable without rewriting the screen
description:
Switching the Palette setting between colour and mono only affects text written afterwards; changing Colors recolours by value (screen_recolour), also hitting ANSI colours equal to a default. Cause: term.c resolves SGR colours to final RGB222 at write time and screen cells store only that.

Design (agreed 2026-10-02, replaces dmt.30):
- Cells (screen_line_t fg/bg, raster_line_t fg/bg) hold an 8-bit xterm-256 palette index; no reserved entries. SGR 39/default fg -> 7, bold default fg -> 15, SGR 49/default bg -> 0. Bold brightens ANSI 0-7 -> 8-15 at write time; reverse swaps indices; 38;5;n stored exactly; 24-bit and RGB -> nearest xterm cube/grey entry. Nothing written depends on the palette.
- Core 1: colour_words grows to 256 RGB565 words (pixel doubled); raster_compose indexes it directly. Two tables, pointer latched at frame start (no half-swapped frame). Palette change = new table, no re-render, no screen_recolour.
- src/palette.[ch] (portable) builds the table from settings (Colors x Palette):
  - White + Colour: 0-15 our ANSI set, 16-255 standard xterm (cube 0/95/135/175/215/255, greys 8+10n).
  - Phosphor (green/amber/blue) + Colour: 0-15 a ramp in the phosphor hue, 16-255 xterm colour.
  - Any + Mono: all 256 entries as a ramp in the hue (white -> grey).
  - Ramp for 0-15 by bands: 0 = 0; 8 ~35%; 4,1,5,2,6,3 ~45-60%; 7 = 67% (today's fg); 12,9,13,10,14,11 ~75-92%; 15 = 100% (today's bold fg). Mono 16-255: luminance mapped into 35-100% (0 only for black).
- main.c picks indices for the status line, SET-UP panel and drive letters per settings (white: 15 on 4; phosphor/mono: 0 on 7) and redraws them in apply_settings as today. term_set_colours, screen_recolour, term_mono_colours, the mono path in term.c go away. Settings record unchanged.
- SET-UP palette preview shows the edited palette live (restore on cancel). Splash keeps its own 4 colours (tint from the hue).
Known trade-offs: default fg == SGR 37 and default bg == SGR 40; similar-luminance colours look alike in mono; phosphor + colour shows ANSI as phosphor but 256/24-bit colours in colour.
acceptance_criteria:
- Switching Colour <-> Mono and changing Colors recolours everything on screen immediately, both directions, without rewriting cells
- 38;5;n shows the exact xterm colour (RGB565); 24-bit maps to the nearest entry
- Status line, SET-UP panel, CP/M console and splash still correct in all 8 Colors x Palette combinations
- Host tests: palette tables, term indices (SGR, bold, reverse, 256/24-bit), raster compose via table; scripts/test.sh and firmware build pass; video_stats().late not worse on hardware
notes: Implemented on branch palette-index (uncommitted): src/palette.[ch] + test_palette; term.c writes indices (TERM_DEFAULT_COLOUR now 0x100, attr fg/bg uint16_t); screen_recolour, term_set_colours/palette, term_mono_colours removed; raster_compose takes a 256-word table; video_set_palette double-buffers, core 1 latches at frame start; settings_colours -> status indices + logo_fg; SET-UP shows the edited palette live (main.c show_palette in setup_service, restored on cancel); demo shows xterm 16-255 swatches. Host tests and firmware build pass; __end__ 0x20077f4c -> 0x200790d8 (+4.4 KB; palette_build is 2.2 KB of code). Phosphor hues (palette.c hues[]): green 33ff33, amber ffb000, blue 3399ff. title: Monitor N (new disk): no progress, slow for 8 MB
description: Creating an 8 MB disk takes a long time and nothing on screen says it is working; when it ends the screen shows the menu heading ('Z80 CP/M machine (z80pack Z80 core)'). Cause: drives_create runs in the main loop and blocks it, so video_update never runs and the 'Writing NAME.DSK...' line is only drawn at the end, together with the menu. It writes 512 bytes per f_write and sdcard.c writes one block per CMD24, so ~16k single-block writes for 8 MB.

Same flush/progress for I (install). Host test: the progress callback fires and the image is complete.
notes: Fixed (uncommitted): monitor flush hook (main: video_update), progress dots per 256 KB for N and I, drives_create writes 16 KB chunks, sdcard.c CMD25 multi-block writes. Host tests pass. Needs hardware check: N 8 MB timing, card still reads back OK.

title: HSTX renderer backend (replace PicoDVI/libdvi)
description: libdvi has no HSTX backend (PIO + SIO TMDS encoders only). Write an HSTX driver behind the same cells+scanline renderer interface (GPIO 12-19 only). Start from pico-examples hstx/dvi_out_hstx_encoder.
design:
GOAL: drive DVI from the RP2350 HSTX (hardware TMDS encoder) instead of PicoDVI's PIO serialisers + software TMDS encode; drop lib/PicoDVI.

KEY RISK: 800x600p60 is 40 MHz pixel clock = 400 Mbps per lane. HSTX shifts 2 bits per clk_hstx (DDR), so clk_hstx = 200 MHz (clk_sys 400 MHz / 2). The datasheet rates clk_hstx to 150 MHz (the pico-examples 640x480 demo runs 125 MHz). 640x480 is not an option (132 cols x 6 px = 792 px). Fallbacks if 200 MHz is unstable: 800x600@56 (36 MHz px, 180 MHz), CVT-RB 800x600 (~35.5 MHz, ~178 MHz). Task .1 settles this on hardware before anything else.

HSTX SETUP (from pico-examples dvi_out_hstx_encoder, adapted): bit[2]/[3] = clock (CLK, INV), lanes 0/1/2 -> bits 0/6/4 with SEL_P/SEL_N = lane*10, lane*10+1, odd bit inverted; CSR CLKDIV 5, N_SHIFTS 5, SHIFT 2, EXPAND_EN. Sync/blanking as HSTX_CMD_RAW_REPEAT control symbols, active pixels as HSTX_CMD_TMDS; command lists + DMA ping-pong (2 chained channels, IRQ on core 1). VESA 800x600p60 timing: H 800/40/128/88, V 600/1/4/23, +hsync +vsync (own table; libdvi's goes away).

PIXEL FORMAT: 16 bpp, EXPAND_TMDS lanes R5/G6/B5 (RGB565), RGB222 levels replicated into the bits (2-bit level 0-3 -> 5-bit 0b00000/01010/10101/11111, 6-bit for green likewise) so full scale is ~0xF8, close to today's levels; 2 px per FIFO word, 1.6 KB per line buffer, 80 MB/s DMA. (8 bpp RGB222 with NBITS 2 would cap brightness at 0xC0.) Confirm levels against the PicoDVI build side by side in .1.

RENDERER (core 1, per scanline, into a ring of ~4 line buffers ahead of DMA): budget 1056 px x 10 = 10560 clk_sys cycles/line at 400 MHz; composing 100-132 cells from a 1bpp ink row + per-cell fg/bg is a few thousand cycles. Cursor = swap fg/bg of the cursor cell on blink-on frames; reverse/blink/bold/underline/connectors stay in raster.c.

RASTER FORMAT (raster.c, portable, host-tested): per line slot, stored rows (font rows + 2 padding) of a 1bpp ink bitmap (800 px = 100 B) + per-cell fg/bg (RGB222 after reverse/attrs). Drops the 2-levels-per-8px-group encoder limit: 132-col colours always exact, and 132 cols no longer has to start on an 8-px boundary (can be centred: 4 px). Memory: ~25 x (18 x 100 + 264) = ~52 KB vs 139 KB raster[] today. The 64-px encoder width, 832-px RASTER_WIDTH and TMDS slack all go.

SPLASH: keep the RLE logo data; copy it to SRAM (core 1 must not touch flash; LOGO_IN_FLASH data copied at splash start into the raster memory), core 1 decodes a row of runs per scanline straight into pixels via a 4-entry tinted palette (replaces splash_row_t, splash_map, splash_colour; splash_tint becomes per-level colours). The 2-levels-per-group limit in logo_gen.py can then be relaxed (follow-up).

MIGRATION: .1 is a standalone test-pattern executable (hstx_test) so the main firmware keeps working; .2-.4 switch the firmware over together (raster format change breaks the libdvi path; no dual-backend period); .5 removes PicoDVI and updates docs. Same video.h API throughout.

title: CP/M BIOSes: second serial port (SIO2, ports 2/3) as READER/PUNCH and AUX:
description:
In CP/M mode the terminal UART is the Z80's SIO2 (ports 2 status / 3 data; machine.c sio2*_in/out -> main.c cpm_aux_in/out -> serial_read/write), but neither BIOS uses it: src/cpm/bios.asm READER returns ^Z and PUNCH/LIST are RET stubs; src/cpm/cpm3/bnkbios3.asm sets @aivec/@aovec to NULL, AUXIST/AUXOST are DEVNRY, AUXIN returns ^Z, CHRTBL lists only TTY1. Only programs poking ports 2/3 directly reach the UART.

Do:
- CP/M 2.2 bios.asm: READER waits on port 2 bit 0 (0 = byte ready, the 88-SIO polarity machine.c sio2s_in returns) and reads port 3; PUNCH writes port 3 (bit 7 0 = ready). LIST stays a stub (no printer; picosim's printer ports 5/6 have no platform hook here).
- CP/M 3 bnkbios3.asm: second device TTY2 in CHRTBL (mb$in$out$serial, baud not selectable), device 1 in the CONIN/CONOUT/AUX* dispatch by vector bit 6 (4000H), AUXIN/AUXOUT default to TTY2 at BOOT (@aivec/@aovec = 4000H) so PIP AUX: and DEVICE work; CONIN/CONOUT can be redirected to it. Rebuilds CPM3.SYS via build.sh (sysgen.run).
- CP/M 2.2 IOBYTE: optional, map RDR:/PUN: values (TTY:/PTR:/PTP:) only if cheap.
- Tests: test_machine boots each system and checks a PIP PUN:= / AUX: copy lands in machine_host aux_sent, and a READER/AUXIN read sees bytes fed to aux_in.
- README: CP/M machine section (ports table 2/3 row) says how to reach the port (PIP, DEVICE).
Flow control on this path is 68t / dmt.27.
notes: Found while reviewing the serial path (2026-10-13): machine.c sio2s_in always reports TX ready (bit 7 = 0), but cpm_aux_out ignores serial_write's return and the TX queue is 256 bytes, so a Z80 writing faster than the baud rate (PIP PUN:/AUX: of a file) loses bytes (counted in serial_stats tx_dropped). Fix with this bead: give the platform an aux_out_ready hook (TX queue has room) and report bit 7 busy from it, so the BIOS's PUNCH/AUXOUT wait. RX side is fine: 2 KB ring, then RTS (flow control builds) or FIFO overrun.

title: USB stick transfers (XPIP USB:) much slower than the SD card
description: Reported by the user on hardware: copying files to/from the USB stick (XLS/XPIP with USB:, FatFs volume 1 via usbmsc.c) is noticeably slower than the same work on the SD card. title: CP/M 3 boot: quiet PROFILE.SUB, SETDEF defaults in the BIOS, README.TXT, CPM32 an 8 MB disk (temporary drive B:)

Cause found: not the console. SUBMIT echoes each line (CR CR LF), each SETDEF prints its setting framed by blank lines, VT100DYN prints ~10 lines: ~36 lines after the loader map on a 23-row screen. Set in BNKBIOS3 BOOT; survives ^C. RMAC: no EQU of external+const, inline works. CPM32 = cpm3-2.dsk files on HD8 via diskimg_gen --convert (Layout class: FD + HD8). README.TXT on CPM31; test follows its ED steps (CP/M 3 ED numbers lines: prompt '    1: *').

title: Boot CP/M 2.2 and CP/M 3 from hard-disk images (design open)
description:
The boot ROM reads track 0 sector 1 of A: whatever its format, but our HD formats have no reserved tracks (DPB OFF 0): track 0 starts the directory, so there is nowhere on the disk for boot sector + CPMLDR.

Preferred: a firmware-resident loader. Build CPMLDR + our LDRBIOS at build time and keep it in flash; when A: is an HD image (port 8 says so) the machine's boot path copies it to 0100H and jumps there instead of reading sector 1. CPMLDR then reads CPM3.SYS as a file from A:, so the disk needs only CPM3.SYS and CCP.COM in its directory. No format change, existing 8 MB images keep working, and any HD with those two files boots. (~3.2 KB of flash.)

Alternative: a new bootable HD format with OFF 1 (one 255-sector track = 32 KB for the loader), told apart by image size (e.g. 8 MB + 32 KB); needs new DPBs in both BIOSes, cpmtools diskdefs, monitor blank-disk support. More moving parts.

Also: a built-in 8 MB CP/M 3 image (CPM3HD: CPM3.SYS, CCP.COM, the DRI utilities, ours) needs diskimg_gen.py to write files into HD-format directories (today --file only does the 8" one); compressed it is mostly E5 runs (LZ4 matches cap at offsets < 4 KB, so ~8 MB / 255 per match of overhead, ~30-40 KB), or create it on the card from a blank HD plus files. CP/M 2.2 could boot from an HD the same way later (a CCP+BDOS+BIOS image in flash, warm boot reloading the CCP from it): out of scope here.
design:
UNDECIDED (2026-10-13 discussion, speculative). Problem: the 4/8 MB formats reserve no tracks (OFF 0); track 0 is directory, so there is no boot sector or system on them.

Options discussed:
A. Firmware boot service behind a ROM stub (FF00 page asks port 8; on an HD the firmware loads CPM3.SYS from the CP/M directory, or a 2.2 image from flash). User prefers nothing special loaded from flash; the 2.2 half needs a BIOS WBOOT change.
B. Bootable HD variants with 2 reserved tracks holding the system in sectors 1-26 of tracks 0-1 (the floppy's layout), so the boot ROM, boot.asm, our WBOOT and picosim's CP/M 3 boot.asm run unchanged. Needs a way to tell the variant apart: by image size (track number is one byte in the FDC command, sector one byte: 256 x 255 is the controller's limit; HD8 already uses it), or by a marker on the disk (see C).
C. Telling bootable from plain by content: byte 0 of track 0 sector 1 (a directory entry starts 0-31, 20H/21H under CP/M 3, or E5; our and picosim's boot sectors start F3 DI) is only a heuristic; a full-signature sector in the reserved area is robust but a private convention. Misdetection shifts the file system by OFF tracks, so it must never guess wrong.

Decide before splitting into work.
close_reason: Dropped: booting from hard-disk images is not needed; CP/M 2.2 and 3 boot from their floppies on A:

title: Decouple clk_sys from the DVI clock (clk_hstx from its own PLL)
description:
clk_sys is 400 MHz only because hstx_dvi_init derives clk_hstx from it (clk_sys/2), a leftover of libdvi's 10x-pixel-clock rule. clk_hstx can come from pll_sys or pll_usb directly, so: pll_sys 400 MHz -> clk_hstx /2 = 200 MHz (pixel clock exactly 40 MHz), pll_usb VCO 1152 -> 384 MHz -> clk_sys (a multiple of 12, so PIO gets an integer /8 = 48 MHz for Pico-PIO-USB) and clk_usb /8 = 48 MHz, clk_peri from clk_sys. Native USB and PIO-USB could then run together. Also makes CPU speed independent of HSTX_MODE (1/2 no longer slow the CPU).

Work: clock bring-up order in hstx_dvi_init (before usbkbd_init); hstx_timing.sys_khz and video_stats' cycle budget (hstx_dvi.c ~240) and diag assume clk_sys = 10 x pixel clock: read actual clocks; check nvflash_retime at the new clk_sys; UART baud follows clk_peri. Core 1 loses ~4% of cycles per line (check the debug status line's compose %). Voltage probably stays 1.3 V.

Deferred: needs hardware with a PIO-USB host port to be worth it (user considering Adafruit Fruit Jam: USB-A hub on PIO-USB GP1/GP2, 5V enable GP11; or PicoTop, which has native USB host and needs none of this). Unblocks a PIO-USB host spike.

title: SET-UP R: reboot the board, back to the boot logo, as a last resort
description:
Why (requested by the user): a last-resort recovery that does not require power-cycling the board. It has to work when the terminal itself is unusable - including when the escape parser is wedged - so it is a local key read by SET-UP, not a byte sent by the host.

Handle it in setup_service() (src/main.c) by reusing the Mode-change pattern already there at src/main.c:392-402: set the message to "Restarting...", draw it, video_update(), drives_flush() if cpm.on, then watchdog_reboot(0, 0, 0) followed by tight_loop_contents(). Add R to the panel's help line.

Note: watchdog_reboot() is a full restart, so it is heavier than it looks - it returns to the boot logo and re-reads the settings, exactly as asked. It also means the terminal state is always clean afterwards, which is why it is the fallback for the freeze tracked in dmt.33.

title: Share one scratch buffer between the monitor (LZ window, blank disks) and the firmware update
description:
SRAM is the tight resource (~32 KB free after .bss in v0.5.0). The monitor's 16 KB 'window' (LZ window for installing disk images, chunk buffer for blank disks) sits idle during a firmware update, while fwupdate.c keeps its own static buffers: 'sector' (4 KB, the commit's copy), 'block' (512 B UF2 block) and 'file' (FIL, ~552 B): about 5 KB.

Make the buffer generic: a small module (e.g. src/scratch.[ch], portable) that owns one static buffer and hands it out through an interface (acquire with a size, release; or a borrow returning pointer+size), with a check that only one user holds it at a time. The monitor's install/new-disk code and fwupdate's check/stage/commit take their memory from it (fwupdate gets it through the monitor platform hooks or by acquiring it itself). The commit must still read nothing from flash: the buffer stays in .bss, and scripts/check_fwupdate.py must still pass.

title: Wider cell colour: xterm 256-colour palette index per cell (after HSTX)
description:
With the HSTX renderer (dmt.8) the display path can show any RGB565 colour per pixel, but screen cells still store fg/bg as RGB222, so SGR 256-colour and 24-bit colours are quantised to 64 colours when written.

title: Flow control as a SET-UP setting: none, RTS/CTS, XON/XOFF
description:
Replace the SERIAL_FLOW_CONTROL build option with a SET-UP setting (saved in flash, applied at runtime like baud/framing from dmt.6) with three choices:

- None (default): GP2/GP3 stay free.
- RTS/CTS: today's hardware flow control on GP3 (RTS out) / GP2 (CTS in), GPIO_FUNC_UART; the RX ring stops draining the FIFO when nearly full so RTS drops. Careful: an unwired CTS can hold TX forever (see VIDEO_DIAG note in main.c); switching pins at runtime must restore them to plain GPIO when leaving RTS/CTS.
- XON/XOFF: receive side sends XOFF (DC3, 0x13) when the RX ring passes a high-water mark and XON (DC1, 0x11) when it drains below a low one (queued ahead of other TX, resent if data keeps arriving); transmit side pauses the TX queue on XOFF from the host and resumes on XON; XON/XOFF bytes are taken out of the received stream rather than passed to the terminal.

Show the mode on the status line (as the RTS/CTS label is now), update README (Flow control section, SET-UP table) and tools/hostbridge.py (--rtscts, add --xonxoff). Host tests for the XON/XOFF logic (portable part split from serial.c), hardware check on the Pico 2.

title: Flash settings store usable at the 400 MHz DVI clock
description: SET-UP (dmt.6) must save settings to flash after video_init has raised clk_sys to 400 MHz. Nothing reads XIP after boot today (COPY_TO_RAM; only the copy loader and binary_info live at 0x10000000), but the SDK flash ops re-run the boot XIP setup, and the ROM routines pick their own SPI divisors, so the SCK rate at 400 MHz has to be checked per chip.
design: RP2350 (bootrom source, varm_generic_flash.c): flash_exit_xip -> flash_init_spi -> flash_enter_cmd_xip sets QMI direct mode and M0/M1 to 03h at CLKDIV 12 (BOOTROM_SPI_CLKDIV_DEFAULT), so ROM erase/program run at 33 MHz at 400 MHz: in spec, no change needed. Afterwards the SDK's flash_enable_xip_via_boot2 replays the boot RAM XIP stub (the mode and divisor the boot found at <=150 MHz, CLKDIV >=3, RXDELAY 2), which is 133 MHz+ at 400 MHz. That is only harmless while nothing reads XIP. Fix: xip_retime() = rom_flash_select_xip_read_mode(BOOTROM_XIP_MODE_03H_SERIAL, ceil(clk_sys/50 MHz)) after set_sys_clock_khz and after every erase/program, so settings can be read back and verified. RP2040 (bootrom program_flash_generic.c): flash_init_spi sets SSI BAUDR=6 (66.7 MHz at 400 MHz, no RX sample delay: same failure class as dmt.10), and it is only called from flash_exit_xip ('makes it possible for user code to edit SPI settings'). Fix: own RAM copy of the SDK erase/program sequence (connect_internal_flash, flash_exit_xip, then ssienr=0 / baudr=16 (25 MHz) / ssienr=1, ROM erase/program, flush_cache, re-enter XIP), then set XIP baudr to 8 as well. Both: call on core 0 without flash_safe_execute or multicore lockout (core 1 and all ISRs are in RAM, and a lockout would stall DVI). Leave IRQs on. A sector erase blocks core 0 for 30-400 ms; the serial RX ring absorbs that. Load settings at boot before video_init (the XIP config from boot is valid then). Store: last 2 flash sectors ping-pong, record = magic, version, seq, len, CRC32, data; newest valid wins, erase only the older sector.
acceptance_criteria: Save in SET-UP at 400 MHz on both targets without DVI dropout; settings survive power cycles; read-back verify passes; a UF2 reflash keeps the settings; power loss during a save leaves the previous settings.
notes: Implemented on branch setup-flash (src/nvflash.[ch], settings.[ch]); host tests + both firmware builds pass. Awaiting hardware check on both boards: save at 400 MHz without DVI dropout, survives power cycle, UF2 reflash keeps settings.
close_reason: Implemented (src/nvflash.[ch], settings.[ch]); verified on the Pico 2 (RP2350): settings save at 400 MHz and persist. RP2040 path built and host-tested only, see follow-up.

title: CP/M 3: settable baud on TTY2 through DEVTBL/DEVINI (DEVICE TTY2 [9600])
description:

title: Quad (EBh) XIP reads for the cold code in flash
description:
Why: since qur.24, cold code (FatFs, TinyUSB's usbh/hub/hid_host/msc_host, the panels, monitor; ~51 KB, ld/section_copy_to_ram_rodata.incl) runs from flash through XIP, which nvflash_retime sets to single-lane 03h at <=50 MHz: ~2 us per XIP cache miss. Quad EBh at the same clock moves 4x the bits per cycle, and continuous-read mode drops the command byte: ~0.3-0.5 us a miss. Only worth doing if the qur.24 hardware measurements (debug status line loop time and Z80 MHz, CP/M disk-heavy work such as a big PIP copy, USB stick I/O) show the slowdown matters.

What: nvflash_retime (src/nvflash.c) picks the mode and divisor in one place, and every flash erase/program already ends in it: rom_flash_select_xip_read_mode(BOOTROM_XIP_MODE_EBH_QUAD, div) instead of 03H_SERIAL.

Checks before switching:
1. Wiring: all four QSPI data lines to the flash. Pico 2: yes. Frankless (boards/frankless.h, bd 59u): very likely (the APS6404L PSRAM shares the bus and needs all four); confirm from its KiCad files.
2. QE bit: Winbond-style parts answer EBh only with QE (status register 2) set; some ship with it set, some not, and the ROM's mode select probably does not set it. Set it at boot with a volatile status write (50h then 31h, no wear) from SRAM before the switch. Check the Pico 2's W25Q32RV and Frankless's 16 MB part.
3. Clock: EBh is rated ~104-133 MHz; at clk_sys 400 MHz a divisor of 4 is 100 MHz and may need QMI rxdelay tuning. Start at 6-8 (50-66 MHz).
4. Other boards: a board header option (e.g. BOARD_FLASH_QUAD, default off = 03h), and/or a read-back check in nvflash_retime (read a known word in 03h, switch, compare through XIP_NOCACHE, fall back to 03h on a mismatch; all from SRAM, so a failed switch cannot hang).
5. PSRAM (g31) on QMI CS1 shares the bus but has its own M1 timing registers.

Measure before and after with the same tests as qur.24. scripts/check_sram_only.py must keep nvflash_retime and its callees in SRAM.

- Add an RTC (DS3231 as on MegaFRANK, or RV-3028/PCF8563) + coin cell on I2C0 GP20/GP21 (or I2C1 GP26/27); a 4-pin I2C header doubles as expansion.

Firmware work once the board exists (file separate beads then):

2. PSRAM per g31: QMI M1 at divider 4 (100 MHz at clk_sys 400 MHz; part rated 133 MHz), QPI 0x35 / read 0xEB / write 0x38, 1 KB page, tCEM 8 us; probe ID at boot and fall back to SRAM banks; Z80 banks >0 in PSRAM (frees 96 KB SRAM), RAM disk, scrollback. Nothing in PSRAM needed during nvflash/fwupdate. Reference: frank-kickstart src/psram_init.c.
3. RTC (optional, probed): machine.c clock ports 65/66 from real time instead of MACHINE_EPOCH_DAYS + uptime; FatFs get_fattime (drop FF_FS_NORTC); status line clock; set via SET-UP and/or a write port for a CP/M DATE tool. Avoid localtime (newlib cost).

description:

title: USB serial port via host CDC (FTDI/CP210x/CH34x/ACM)
description: Optional serial port through a USB-serial adapter on the host port (behind a hub), for boards without a UART with CTS/RTS (e.g. picoTop). Analysis 2026-10-07: TinyUSB 0.18 CDC host + FTDI/CP210x/CH34x drivers + 1 KB RX FIFO cost ~7.4 KB SRAM (__end__ 0x20079ac8 -> 0x2007b848). Needs CFG_TUH_HUB 2, one more device slot; endpoints fit (15 async). Risks: RX only advances in tuh_task (main loop), so CP/M slices/renders/SD I/O can overflow the adapter's FIFO; TinyUSB never enables the adapter's RTS/CTS, so we must send vendor requests (FTDI SET_FLOW_CTRL, CP210x SET_FLOW, CH34x reg) from the main loop after all devices mount (qur.3 rule), same for line coding on SET-UP changes; CDC notifications (DCD/DSR/RI) unhandled in 0.18. serial.c would get a UART/CDC backend switch; terminal and CP/M SIO2 then use it unchanged. Preferred alternative: a 4-pin hardware UART block (aligned GPIO group TX/RX/CTS/RTS).

title: XON/XOFF software flow control (SET-UP setting, terminal mode)
description:
The RP2350's UARTs (PL011) only do RTS/CTS in hardware; XON/XOFF has to be in serial.c.

Receive: when the RX ring passes a threshold, send XOFF (0x13); XON (0x11) where serial_read resumes. Both bypass the TX queue (written straight to the UART ahead of queued bytes). Threshold much earlier than the RTS one (64 bytes left): the host's driver and USB-serial adapter keep sending a few hundred bytes after XOFF, so pause at ~half the 2 KB ring, and keep draining the FIFO after XOFF (unlike the RTS path, which leaves bytes in the FIFO).

Transmit: the IRQ filters 0x11/0x13 out before the ring and sets a flag serial_poll checks; up to 32 bytes already in the TX FIFO still go out.

Trade-off: Ctrl-S/Ctrl-Q stop being data (Emacs, WordStar keys, XMODEM), so a SET-UP setting (Flow: none / XON/XOFF; one new byte in the append-only settings record), off by default, terminal mode only (in CP/M mode the UART is the Z80's SIO2 and programs need every byte). RTS/CTS stays a build option. Put the filter/threshold logic in a small portable module for host tests; hardware check against a real host's buffering.

Also: README's Flow control section says 4 KB receive buffer; it is 2 KB since qur.23.

title: Spike: 8 MB QSPI PSRAM on QMI CS1 (Z80 banks, RAM disk, scrollback)
description:
Spike: what 8 MB (64 Mbit) of QSPI PSRAM on QMI CS1 would take and buy. Not scheduled; revisit when hardware changes (a custom board for this project, or the Adafruit Feather RP2350 variant with spare pads for a PSRAM IC).

Audit, 2026-10-04 (main c6fb393): __end__ 0x200796a0, ~26.3 KB SRAM free; flash image 504 KB of the 2 MB region. The limit is Z80 memory in 48 KB chunks: a third bank, a RAM disk or scrollback do not fit in SRAM.

Buys:
- Z80 banks: simmem.h reaches non-zero banks through curbnk, so pointing banks at PSRAM (0x11000000 window) is nearly a one-line change. Keep bnk0 + the common area in SRAM so CP/M 2.2 sees no slowdown; only banked programs (MP/M, CP/M 3) touch PSRAM. Moving today's 2 banks frees 96 KB of SRAM; 8 MB holds 100+ banks.
- RAM disk (e.g. 4 MB M: drive), terminal scrollback (~25k 80-col lines), bigger transfer/USB copy buffers.

Does not buy: anything core 1 or the video reads (800x600x60 RGB565 needs ~58 MB/s; QSPI peaks ~50 MB/s and shares the 16 KB XIP cache with flash; core 1 must stay off XIP). No help to cpx.

Hardware options:
1. Custom board: PSRAM on the QSPI bus, CS1 on a free pin.
2. Adafruit Feather RP2350 variant with spare PSRAM pads (check its CS1 pin against our pin map and the DVI wiring).
3. Pico-footprint board with PSRAM (e.g. Pimoroni Pico Plus 2, RP2350B, CS1 GP47); check DVI Sock pins GP12-19 line up.
4. Plain Pico 2: piggyback an APS6404L on the flash, CS1 to GP8 (QSPI lines are not on the header). Delicate.

Questions for the spike:
- QMI M1 timing at clk_sys 400 MHz (divider >= 4, ~100 MHz; APS6404L page-wrap and tCEM limits), set independently of nvflash_retime's slow CS0 timing.
- nvflash and fwupdate_commit: do the ROM/SDK flash calls keep CS1 configured (SDK saves/restores QMI CS1)? Nothing in PSRAM may be needed during a flash operation; the fwupdate checker must still pass.
- Z80 speed with banks in PSRAM (cache misses cost a few hundred cycles); measure with the speed test and the exercisers.
- Board detection: probe the PSRAM at boot (ID read) and fall back to SRAM banks when absent, so one firmware works on both boards.

title: Bug fixes: deferred and low-priority defects
description: Holding epic for known bugs that are deferred or not tied to a feature pass: hard-to-reproduce hardware sightings and compatibility fixes for other machines. Pick these up when a reproduction or a quiet stretch turns up.

title: Raster: derive the padding rows instead of storing them (~5 KB SRAM)
description: Each raster line stores font rows + 2 padding rows (22 x 100 bytes in 80 columns); 132 columns never shows padding scanlines (6x12 doubled fills the 24-scanline row). The padding rows are just the first/last glyph row ANDed with a per-cell connector mask (glyph_is_connector). Store a connector bit mask per line (100 bytes, or per-cell bits) and have raster_compose (core 1) AND it in on the 4 padding scanlines of each 80-column row, dropping 2 stored rows per slot: 25 x 200 bytes = ~5 KB. Costs core 1 a few cycles per cell on those scanlines only (80 columns is at ~62% of the line budget). Low priority: only if SRAM gets tight again.

title: Speculative: run cold code from flash (XIP) to free ~25-35 KB of SRAM
description: Speculative, needs a plan before any code. Everything runs from SRAM (COPY_TO_RAM: .text ~170 KB). Cold code could execute from flash through XIP once nvflash_retime has set the 03h read mode for 400 MHz: FatFs (~10 KB), USB enumeration (usbh/hub/hid_host ~9 KB), monitor, drivepanel, setup, fwpanel, demo, palette_build, qsort, printf (~6 KB). Constraints: nothing from flash between set_sys_clock (video_init) and nvflash_retime; nothing from flash during flash erase/program (nvflash ops, settings saves, fwupdate staging; core 0 IRQ handlers must stay in RAM); fwupdate_commit_image must stay RAM-only (scripts/check_fwupdate.py); core 1 never touches flash. XIP is single-lane 03h at 50 MHz (~2 us per cache miss): hot paths (Z80 core, term/vtparse, raster, sdcard, serial) stay in SRAM. Consider quad (EBh) XIP if it can be set up safely at 400 MHz. Mechanism to look at: pico-sdk __in_flash()/.flashtext sections, or per-object section renames in CMake. Measure with the debug status line (loop time, Z80 MHz) before and after.
notes: 2026-10-12 hardware (user): works. Debug status line: main loop idles ~10 ms, render ~100-103 us (steady); loop peaks up to ~460 ms while USB devices are plugged/unplugged (enumeration/stick mount, usbh/hub/msc_host now in flash; no same-session baseline from the all-SRAM build). If enumeration stalls matter, cpx.2 (quad XIP) or moving usbh back to SRAM.

title: Plan: draw glyphs on core 1 from the screen buffer, dropping the 61.6 KB raster cache
description: Speculative planning ticket. Today core 0 pre-renders every line into raster memory (raster_line_t x 25 = 61.6 KB, the biggest SRAM user after the Z80 banks) and core 1 only expands bits to pixels. Core 1 could instead read cells (glyph, fg, bg, attr) and the font directly per scanline. Costs/risks: the fonts core 1 reads must be in SRAM (all tables ~31 KB incl. 10x20 + bolds; core 1 must never touch flash), bold/underline/blink/reverse/connector padding per scanline, cursor, the splash (uses raster memory as its buffer today), and the per-line budget (10,560 cycles at 400 MHz; video_stats().late). Net SRAM maybe ~30 KB. Worth it only if something big needs the memory (e.g. a third Z80 bank: 48 KB). Output: measurements (cycle count of a compose prototype on hardware with VIDEO_DIAG) and a go/no-go.
close_reason: Not viable: core 1 already uses 87-92% of the scanline in 132 columns (qur.22); drawing glyphs there would overrun. Decided 2026-10-03.

title: WORMS: detect the machine before touching clock ports (hangs on fz80, writes its disk port)
description: On the fz80 (fz80-firmware), WORMS hangs in CALIB: ports 65/66 are the fz80 disk controller's DSK_LOW/HIGH_ADDR (0x41/0x42); IN 0x42 is unhandled and returns 0, so CAL1 waits forever for the seconds to change (no BDOS calls, so no key gets out; reset needed). OUT (65) in CALIB and SEED also overwrites the low byte of the fz80's disk parameter block address. No CPR reply there either (cursor left bottom right; GETC timeout handles that).
design:
Pick a time source without blind OUTs:
1. BDOS 12: MP/M (01xxh) -> function 141 Delay (system ticks, fz80 50 Hz); CP/M 3 (31h) -> function 105 time to calibrate.
2. Else probe IN A,(50h) (read-only on both): 01h = fz80 (RTC_STATUS_PORT returns RTC_DONE_MASK) -> RTC millis counter (OUT (50h),2 then 4 reads of 51h), seed from PRNG port 70h; FFh = picosim/ours (unused port, IO_DATA_UNUSED) -> existing 65/66 clock, optionally confirm IN 65 in {0,1} and IN 66 BCD seconds; anything else -> no clock: fixed UNITMS, seed from R only, no OUTs.
3. Bound CAL1/CAL3 so a clock that never ticks cannot hang (fall back to fixed UNITMS).
Avoid: IN 64 (fz80 0x40 disk status read clears the result), other fz80 status reads that clear state; tick interrupts (too invasive for a .COM).
acceptance_criteria: WORMS runs on the fz80 without hanging and without writing disk ports; unchanged behaviour on the dvi-terminal CP/M machine; host tests pass.

title: Z80 core: undocumented X/Y flags (F bits 3/5) not modelled
description: CPUTEST (SuperSoft Diagnostics II) on Z80TESTS fails test 0025h: INC C (0C) leaves F=00H where a real Z80 gives 08H (bit 3 copied from the result). z80pack's Z80 cores (simz80*.c and ALT_Z80 altz80.h) never set X_FLAG/Y_FLAG: they model documented flags only, so EXZ80DOC passes but CPUTEST/ZEXALL do not. CP/M software rarely depends on these bits. Options: accept; patch z80pack (local patch or upstream PR); or swap in a core that models them (e.g. Superzazu z80, floooh chips) behind machine.c.
design: X/Y set in the vendored core via SET_XY/SET_XY_BLOCK (simdefs.h): result for ALU/INC/DEC/shifts/NEG/DAA/RLD/RRD/IN/LD A,I/R; CP's operand; BIT r: r, BIT (IX/IY+d): address high byte, BIT (HL): unchanged (no MEMPTR); SCF/CCF/CPL/RLCA..RRA: A; ADD HL/IX/IY,rr and ADC/SBC HL: high byte; LDI/LDD: byte+A, CPI/CPD: A-(HL)-H (bits 1/3). EXZ80ALL.COM (+ .MAC) added to Z80TESTS. Host: EXZ80DOC, EXZ80ALL all tests successful, CPUTEST 'CPU TESTS OK' (CPU_TESTS=1, ~3 min). CPUTEST stops at its first failure, so more X/Y differences may follow once this one is fixed. ALT_Z80 fails the same test (no X/Y either).

The HSTX renderer (dmt.8) decodes per pixel, so the limit only costs image quality. title: Terminal type setting: VT100 or ADM-3A
description: Split out of dmt.6 ('later VT100/ADM-3A mode'): a SET-UP setting choosing the emulation, VT100 (default) or Lear Siegler ADM-3A (ESC = row col cursor addressing, ^Z clear, ^K/^L/^H/^J cursor moves, no attributes), for CP/M software configured for an ADM-3A. Related: dmt.16 (VT52 mode).
notes:
Evaluation (2026-10-09). Cheap and low risk: portable, host-testable, no video/core 1 change, ~1-1.5 KB SRAM. Not a superset of VT100, so it needs its own decoder (do the personality split first: see the blocking refactor task).

Conflicts with the VT100 path: ^K/^L are LF in VT100 (term.c execute) but cursor up / non-destructive right in ADM-3A; ESC = is DECKPAM vs cursor address ESC = row+32 col+32; ^Z (SUB) cancels a sequence vs clear+home; ^^ (0x1E) home. So term_write sends bytes to a small ADM state machine (normal / ESC / row / col) instead of vtparse_byte, reusing print, move_to, index_down and the erase helpers (~100-150 lines). CP/M mode gets it for free (cpm_console_out goes through term_write); that is the main use.

Details:
- Wrap: ADM-3A wraps as soon as the last column is written (terminfo adm3a: am, no xenl) and writing the bottom-right cell scrolls; VT100's deferred wrap must be off in this mode.
- Keyboard (keyboard.c editing_key): arrows send ^K up, ^J down, ^H left, ^L right; Home ^^; other editing/function keys nothing; F11/F12 unchanged. One flag in kbd_modes_t (or a per-personality key map).
- Settings trap: payload byte 11 still holds the retired layout (0/1) in old records. Encode the new field as {0 VT100, 2 ADM-3A} so an old 1 is invalid and settings_decode falls back to VT100. Test that.
- SET-UP: one more row, SETUP_ROWS 18 -> 19 of 24 (Drives/fwpanel static_asserts still hold), ~528 B more saved-row buffer.
- 80 columns only in ADM mode (bias-32 7-bit addressing tops out at col 95; the ADM-3A is 80x24).
- Lost in ADM mode: colours/attributes, DA/CPR replies, host CSI ? 999 ~ SET-UP request (would print as text unless special-cased). Gained: no vtparse OSC/DCS sink-state hang.
- Scope suggestion: include Kaypro-style extras ESC T (clear EOL), ESC Y (clear EOS), ESC E / ESC R (insert/delete line) - check against a Kaypro manual first. Plain ADM-3A has no clear-EOL, so software redraws with spaces.
- dmt.16 (VT52) has the same decoder shape (ESC Y bias-32 addressing); build both on the personality split.
- Tests: test_term cases for the controls, immediate wrap, bottom-right scroll; settings test for the byte-11 value.
Replies per personality (user, 2026-10-09: make sure the right answer-back responses happen): VT100 DA/DECID ESC [ ? ... c, DSR/CPR, DECREQTPARM; VT52 sub-mode ESC Z -> ESC / Z; ADM-3A sends nothing (no DA/CPR/ENQ answerback), so the reply path must not emit VT100 replies in ADM mode. Check ENQ answerback (currently none) is consistent across modes.
Done 2026-10-09 on branch adm3a: src/adm3a.c. Checked against terminfo adm3a/kaypro (am without xenl -> immediate wrap; cup bias 32; Kaypro el ^X, ed ^W, il1 ESC E, dl1 ESC R) and retrocmp.de's Kaypro table. Edge stops for ^K/^L and clamping of out-of-range ESC = are our choice (manual scan unreadable here). 8th bit stripped (parity; WordStar). Found while doing it: SET-UP/Drives panel/monitor parse ESC [ x keys, so VT52 (and ADM) key encoding broke them - fixed on term-split (c9bc193): firmware UIs always get VT100 ANSI keys.

title: Keep the startup logo in flash instead of resident SRAM
description: Nice to have. With COPY_TO_RAM the 19 KB RLE logo (generated logo.c 'data') is copied to SRAM at boot and stays there, though it is only used at power-on/reset; on the RP2040 that is a large share of the ~22 KB heap headroom. Since nvflash_retime() keeps XIP readable at 400 MHz (03h <= 50 MHz), place the logo data in a flash-only section (e.g. __in_flash()) and let splash_unpack (core 0) read it via XIP; core 1 never touches it. Check: RP2040 XIP retime path (depends on dmt.24 hardware check), logo still shows on both boards, __end__ moves down ~19 KB in the RP2040 .elf.map, unpack time acceptable at 50 MHz serial reads.

title: Smooth scrolling (DECSCLM, CSI ? 4 h)
description: DECSCLM is parsed and ignored: all scrolling is jump scrolling. VT100 smooth scroll moves the scrolling region up/down a scanline at a time (about 6 lines/s at 60 Hz) and holds off the host meanwhile. Needs: a per-region pixel offset in core 1's scanline -> stored-row mapping (cheap: rows are already per-slot buffers), the emulator queueing scrolls while one animates, and flow control to the host (RTS/CTS or XON/XOFF from dmt.4), since 115200 baud outruns 6 lines/s at once. Found in vttest on hardware (build 50c447b).

title: Optional: keyboard over PIO-USB on pio1 to keep USB CDC console
description: Pico-PIO-USB fully on pio1 (libdvi owns pio0 SM0-2, 6 DMA ch, PWM slice 0). Set tx_ch explicitly (default 0 collides with DVI). 252 MHz is 21x12 MHz OK. SOF IRQ on core0 at top priority. Unproven combination: prototype early.
close_reason: Not viable: 800x600 runs clk_sys at 400 MHz, not a multiple of 12 MHz as Pico-PIO-USB needs, and it would cost more CPU/RAM than the native controller on the RP2040 that already failed (dmt.20). The native-port keyboard (dmt.5) covers RP2350.
